extracted.intended_audience: preprint server operators, research infrastructure managers, bibliometricians, and open-research stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and recommending which bibliographic metadata elements preprint servers should deposit to Crossref, and evaluating the completeness of those deposits across servers. Focuses on pragmatic minimums, ideal practices, and observed coverage for key metadata fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOI registration and mandatory metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprint servers register DOIs at Crossref; depositing the title and the publication date of a preprint is mandatory, while other metadata elements are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each preprint has a DOI and that at minimum title and publication date are deposited to Crossref. Use DOI registration as the baseline requirement for discoverability and linking; recognize other fields may be optional but are valuable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a preprint's Crossref metadata includes the reference list. Inclusion varies strongly by server: bioRxiv, medRxiv, and JMIR Preprints generally include references; SSRN and Research Square include them unevenly (SSRN missing for >50%); many servers (Preprints.org, Authorea, TechRxiv, ChemRxiv, OSF-hosted servers like PsyArXiv and SocArXiv) do not include reference lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideally preprint servers should deposit full reference lists to Crossref to improve citation-linking and discoverability, but collecting and formatting references can be resource-intensive. Treat reference deposition as an 'ideal' enhancement when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of the preprint abstract in Crossref metadata. Almost all preprint servers include abstracts in the metadata they submit, though some (e.g., Authorea, TechRxiv) have significant gaps and SSRN does not include abstracts in Crossref metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts are considered a basic metadata element and should be submitted to Crossref; they substantially aid discoverability and indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCIDs
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of ORCID iDs in Crossref metadata for at least one author of a preprint. Most servers include an ORCID for at least one author, but SSRN provides none and Research Square includes ORCIDs only for a small share of preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit ORCIDs to Crossref, ideally for all authors. ORCIDs improve author disambiguation and interoperability across systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether author affiliation information is included in Crossref metadata. Most preprint servers do not include affiliations or include them only for a small share; exceptions with high coverage are Research Square, Authorea, and ChemRxiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, include the affiliation of the corresponding author; ideally include affiliations for all authors. Use standardized identifiers (e.g., ROR) where possible to improve interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding information
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of funding acknowledgements / funder metadata in Crossref records. Only a few servers include funding information: ChemRxiv (about 40% coverage) and EGUsphere (about 75%). bioRxiv has recently begun collecting and submitting funding data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include funding information when available to support transparency and tracking of funder outputs; recognize that collection may require additional workflow changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: License information
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of license metadata (e.g., CC licenses) in Crossref deposits. Most preprint servers include license information, but notable exceptions are SSRN and JMIR Preprints; Authorea includes it only for a small share, and bioRxiv/medRxiv historically had minority coverage but are improving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License information should be deposited as a basic metadata element because it directly affects reuse. Servers should prioritize making license metadata available for new and legacy records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness of bibliographic metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic metadata deposited to Crossref is made openly available, aligning with open-research declarations such as the Barcelona Declaration on Open Research Information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deposit metadata openly to Crossref to enable discovery and reuse by bibliographic databases and tools; openness is framed as a community good that supports a mature preprint ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR metadata practices and standardized identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Metadata should support FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable). The post highlights moves such as OSF migrating from FundRef to ROR for institutional affiliations to standardize and strengthen affiliation metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt persistent, standardized identifiers (ORCID for authors, ROR for organizations, standard funder IDs) and structured metadata formats to enhance interoperability and reuse. This helps downstream services ingest and link records reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended minimal vs. ideal metadata submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors recommend a practical minimum set of metadata and an ideal target: at least submit the abstract and license information plus the ORCID and affiliation of the corresponding author; ideally also submit reference lists, funding information, and ORCIDs and affiliations for all authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the minimum set as a realistic baseline for resource-limited servers, and target the ideal set as resources or tooling improve. Explicitly acknowledge resource constraints while planning incremental improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating versions and DOIs as separate records
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple versions of a preprint exist on a server and each has its own DOI, each version should be treated as a separate preprint record in Crossref-derived statistics and systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register DOIs per version where appropriate and ensure metadata for each version is deposited and kept accurate; downstream systems should account for versioning when aggregating or counting preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Crossref as the ingestion source for preprint bibliographic metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Crossref can serve as a central infrastructure to improve the availability of preprint metadata to bibliographic databases and tools, because many preprint servers deposit DOIs and metadata there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic databases and discovery tools should ingest preprint metadata from Crossref to make metadata broadly available; preprint servers should prioritize Crossref deposition to maximize downstream visibility.
